name: South Indian Veg Kurma
equipment: Kadai or heavy pan with a lid: the base of the whole dish
Mixer-grinder (small jar) or hand blender for the smooth paste
Chopping board and knife, small bowl for soaking, measuring spoons, kitchen scale
A spoon or a fork for testing the vegetables

steps.title: Soak the cashews
steps.text: Put 4 cashews (6 g) in a small bowl with 2 tbsp hot water.
steps.visualCue: Cashews look plump and slightly soft, and the water turns faintly cloudy
steps.cameraCheck: The bowl of cashews in water
steps.watchOut: Using cold water, so the cashews stay hard and the paste turns grainy; if short of time, use hot water and soak 5 min, or add 2 more minutes of blending.

steps.title: Dice the hard vegetables
steps.text: Cut 40 g potato and 30 g carrot into 1 cm cubes.
steps.visualCue: Even cubes about the size of a green pea cluster, all the same size
steps.cameraCheck: The cubes on the board next to a coin
steps.watchOut: Cubes of mixed sizes: small ones turn to mush while big ones stay raw in the middle; re-cut the large pieces so they match.

steps.title: Cut the beans and cauliflower, and measure the peas
steps.text: Cut 25 g beans into 1 cm pieces, 30 g cauliflower into small florets, and put 20 g peas in a bowl.
steps.visualCue: Beans and florets roughly the same size as the carrot cubes
steps.cameraCheck: All the chopped vegetables in one bowl
steps.watchOut: Large cauliflower florets that fall apart before the stem is soft; cut the stem ends thin.

steps.title: Slice the onion and chop the tomato
steps.text: Slice 40 g onion thin and chop 40 g tomato small.
steps.visualCue: Thin, even onion half-rings and small red tomato pieces
steps.cameraCheck: The sliced onion and chopped tomato
steps.watchOut: Thick onion slices that stay chunky and make the gravy uneven; slice thin or the onion will not melt into the sauce.

steps.title: Prepare the aromatics
steps.text: Grate or crush 2 g ginger and 2 g garlic fine, and slit or chop 1 green chilli (3 g).
steps.visualCue: A small wet pile of ginger and garlic; the smell is sharp and fresh
steps.cameraCheck: The ginger, garlic and chilli on the board
steps.watchOut: Large garlic bits that burn quickly in the pan; crush them fine so they cook in seconds.

steps.title: Grind the paste
steps.text: Put 25 g coconut, the soaked cashews (drained), 4 g roasted gram dal, 1 g fennel and the green chilli in a small mixer jar with 60 ml water. Grind to a smooth paste.
steps.visualCue: A smooth, pale, creamy paste with no visible coconut shreds; it smells sweet from the fennel
steps.cameraCheck: The paste in the jar, held up so you can see it is smooth
steps.videoShot: Paste swirling and smoothing in the jar.
steps.watchOut: A gritty, watery paste from too little blending or too much water; scrape down the jar and blend 30 sec more.
steps.funFact: South Indian kurma is built on a fresh coconut and seed paste, while North Indian korma uses a yogurt, nut and fried-onion base (Swasthi's Indian Healthy Recipes).

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Put the kadai on medium heat, add 6 g (1½ tsp) sunflower oil and warm it for 30 sec.
steps.visualCue: The oil looks thin and shimmers when you tilt the pan
steps.cameraCheck: The pan with the shimmering oil
steps.watchOut: Smoking oil, which makes the spices bitter; if it smokes, take the pan off the heat for 20 sec.

steps.title: Temper the whole spices
steps.text: Add the bay leaf, 1 cm cinnamon, 2 cloves and 1 cardamom pod. Stir for 20–30 sec.
steps.visualCue: A sweet, warm spice smell and the cloves puff slightly
steps.videoShot: Whole spices sizzling in the oil.
steps.watchOut: Dark, scorched spices and a bitter smell; they need only half a minute, so move on straight away to the onion.

steps.title: Cook the onion
steps.text: Add the sliced onion and a pinch of salt. Cook on medium for 4–5 min, stirring, until soft and light golden.
steps.visualCue: Onions turn translucent, then pale gold, and smell sweet
steps.watchOut: Dark brown edges, which make the kurma look and taste heavy (a white-ish gravy is the aim); lower the heat and add a spoon of water if they colour too fast.

steps.title: Add ginger, garlic and chilli
steps.text: Add the crushed ginger and garlic and stir for 30 sec.
steps.visualCue: The raw sharp smell turns warm and savoury
steps.watchOut: Garlic that browns and goes bitter; keep stirring and move to the tomato at once.

steps.title: Cook the tomato
steps.text: Add the chopped tomato and cook 3 min, mashing it with the spoon, until soft and pulpy.
steps.visualCue: The tomato melts into a thick pulp and oil gathers faintly at the edges
steps.cameraCheck: The mashed tomato in the pan
steps.watchOut: Tomato that is still in chunks and sour; keep cooking and mash with the back of the spoon.

steps.title: Add the powders
steps.text: Reduce the heat to low. Add 0.5 g turmeric, 1.5 g coriander powder and 0.5 g Kashmiri chilli powder and stir for 20 sec.
steps.visualCue: The mixture turns deep yellow-orange and smells toasty
steps.watchOut: Powders that stick and burn on a dry pan, with a sharp acrid smell; add 1 tbsp water straight away to rescue it.

steps.title: Cook the vegetables
steps.text: Add the potato, carrot, beans, cauliflower and peas, 1.5 g (¼ tsp) salt and 150 ml water. Bring to a boil, cover, lower the heat and simmer 10 min.
steps.tip: The lid keeps the steam in, so the vegetables cook evenly without extra water.
steps.visualCue: A knife or fork tip goes into the potato and carrot with slight resistance; the vegetables keep their colour and shape
steps.cameraCheck: A fork piercing a potato cube
steps.videoShot: Colourful vegetables simmering under the lid.
steps.watchOut: Raw, hard potato (too short) or mush (too long); test a potato cube at 8 min, and if the pan dries, add 2 tbsp hot water.

steps.title: Stir in the coconut paste
steps.text: Add the paste with 50 ml water. Stir, then simmer on low for 4–5 min, uncovered or half-covered, stirring now and then. Do not boil hard.
steps.visualCue: The gravy turns creamy off-white to pale yellow and thickens enough to coat the spoon; the raw coconut smell goes
steps.cameraCheck: The gravy coating the back of the spoon
steps.watchOut: Hard boiling, which splits the coconut paste and leaves oily specks (Archana's Kitchen warns not to boil the kurma again after the paste goes in); if it splits, lower the heat and whisk in 2 tbsp warm water.

steps.title: Finish and rest
steps.text: Switch off the heat. Stir in 0.5 g garam masala, taste and add a pinch of salt if needed, then scatter 2 g chopped coriander leaves. Cover and rest 2 min.
steps.visualCue: A glossy, creamy gravy, thick but pourable, with vegetables in it and a sweet spice and coconut smell
steps.watchOut: A gravy that is too thick or too thin (it thickens as it cools): add a splash of hot water if it is thick, or simmer 1 min more on low if it is runny.

reasons: about 145 g of vegetables in one bowl, a plant-only recipe with no cholesterol, no frying of the vegetables, only 6 g oil, and a good 8 g of fibre. Points off for saturated fat of about 8.6 g (39% of a daily limit, nearly all from coconut), sodium of about 630 mg and low protein (about 8 g). Restaurant versions commonly add more oil, cream, ghee or curd and extra salt, and are served with fried parotta, so a bowl of 350–450 kcal with more saturated fat is common (est.).

researchRating.basis: a very widely published South Indian staple. Indian Healthy Recipes, Hebbar's Kitchen, Cook With Manali, Yummy Tummy, Chitra's Food Book, Archana's Kitchen, Vidhya's Home Cooking and Jeyashri's Kitchen all publish it, usually described as the mild, creamy side for parotta, idli, dosa and chapati. Points off because recipes vary a lot (with or without poppy seeds, curd or coconut milk), the gravy is easy to split, and it is rarely eaten on its own. Recipe-site star counts were not checked this run. Platform dish ratings were not used.

storage: Fridge-safe in a closed box for up to 2 days (cool within 1 hour). Freezing is not recommended: the potato turns grainy and the coconut gravy can split on thawing. Reheat in a pan on low with 2–3 tbsp water, stirring gently, until just steaming; do not boil hard. The gravy thickens overnight, so loosen it.
leftoverRemix: Kurma dosa roll. Cook the leftover kurma down until it is thick and almost dry, mash lightly, and use it as the filling for a crisp plain dosa or a toasted chapati roll with a little green chutney and sliced onion.
burnOff: about 4.3 km of running (300 ÷ 70 kcal/km, for a 70 kg adult), or about 6 km of brisk walking (about 1 h 12 min at 5 km/h, using about 50 kcal/km for walking) (est.). With 2 chapatis (about 480 kcal): about 6.9 km running or 9.6 km walking (est.).

navratri.reason: onion, garlic, garam masala, table salt and the roasted gram (a pulse) are out under the common rule set; use sendha namak, keep potato, carrot, coconut and cashew, and leave out peas, beans, cauliflower and the chana dal (assumption: the common rule set; families differ).

ekadashi.reason: no grain in the dish, but peas, beans and roasted gram are legumes and onion and garlic are avoided; cook only potato, carrot, coconut and cashew with sendha namak (common rule set).

jain.reason: onion, garlic, fresh ginger, potato and carrot are roots; cook the Jain variant.

ramadan.reason: vegetarian, so no halal-meat issue; moderate sodium (about 630 mg) and not very heavy, a good side for parotta or idiyappam at iftar dinner and fine at sehri with idli.

jain.reason: the main recipe uses onion, garlic, fresh ginger, potato and carrot; cook the Jain variant (no roots, sonth and hing).

vegan.reason: no dairy, ghee, honey or egg; the fat is sunflower oil and coconut (hotel versions sometimes add curd, cream or ghee).

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, so no meat or egg; no fish needed.

sattvik.reason: the main recipe uses onion 40 g and garlic 2 g; cook the Sattvik variant.

glutenFree.reason: no wheat, rava or maida, and the recipe uses no hing. Check the garam masala label for added flour; most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour, so use gluten-free hing if you add any.

dairyFree.reason: no milk, curd, ghee, cream or paneer in the main recipe (restaurant versions may add cream or curd).
